title: material fissure
definition: A narrow physical discontinuity extends through or along a material bearer where the material on either side would otherwise be joined. It may be internal or visible at a surface.
example: A fissure runs through the ceramic.
near: A painted line on intact ceramic.
reuse: A cracked object bears one of these discontinuities.

title: material object bearing a fissure
definition: A particular material object currently bears at least one material fissure. The fissure belongs to that object. The object may still function and need not have separated into pieces.
example: Pip found a cracked bell that could still ring.
near: The bell fails because its clapper is missing but its material is intact.
reuse: The same restriction can describe a radio, a bell or the subject of another action.

title: episode of physical oscillation
definition: During one reported episode a material bearer moves back and forth about a position. The episode includes repeated reversals. Audible emission, a receiver and a communicative intention are optional.
example: Her phone vibrated silently.
near: The phone slid once across the table.
reuse: An emitting vibration provides the mechanical source for a sound.

title: episode of mechanical sound emission
definition: Oscillation in a material source sends a mechanical pressure or elastic wave into a surrounding medium during the same episode. No listener or intention to signal is required.
example: An alarm sounded in an empty room.
near: An earpiece detected a wave from elsewhere without emitting it.
reuse: A source that rings emits this kind of sound with sustained resonance.

title: episode of resonant ringing
definition: One source produces a resonant ringing sound during an episode of mechanical sound emission. The ringing is the sound of that source. A listener, a responsible striker and repeated strikes are unspecified.
example: The bell rang in the empty hall.
near: Someone rang Ada on the phone to speak with her.
reuse: Restrictions on which sources rang can be quantified independently.

title: another occurrence of a pattern
definition: An occurrence of a pattern takes place again after a prior occurrence of that same pattern. The newer occurrence is distinct. The interval, exact repetition count and cause are unspecified.
example: The retries recurred.
near: One uninterrupted retry continued for a longer time.
reuse: Causing a recurrence adds the participant who brings about the later occurrence.

title: cause another occurrence of a pattern
definition: One participant brings about a later occurrence of the specified earlier pattern. The two occurrences instantiate the same pattern. The cause of the first occurrence may be different.
example: The arrival repeated the pulse.
near: A pulse recurred without being brought about by the named participant.
reuse: A replay can add the restriction that a recorded sequence supplies the pattern.

title: cessation of an occurrence
definition: A previously ongoing occurrence reaches an endpoint at which its continuation ceases. The resulting situation begins at that endpoint. No destruction, lasting inactivity or deliberate agent is implied.
example: The pulse ceased.
near: The pulse became quieter while it continued.
reuse: A pause adds the possibility of continuing the same activity after an interval.

title: arrival back at a prior position
definition: A mover reaches a place it occupied earlier. The place reached is the earlier place of this same mover. The route, duration away and reason for coming back are unspecified.
example: The cart returned to its former position.
near: The pulse happened again without travelling back to an earlier position.
reuse: A round trip can add a departure from that same place.

title: interval of deferred action
definition: During an interval a participant defers a pending action while a condition or occasion for acting is outstanding. Other activity can continue. The pending action need never actually happen.
example: The counter waited.
near: A counter stopped existing or never had a pending action.
reuse: Waiting for a particular event can specify the outstanding condition.

title: fault that impairs an intended function
definition: An object or process has a manifest fault that interferes with at least one of its intended functions under the conditions where that function is expected. Other functions can remain available.
example: A faulty chair drops when someone leans back.
near: A chair has a harmless scratch and every intended function works.
reuse: Functional breakage adds that an intended function can no longer be performed as required.

title: functionally broken object or process
parts: fault that impairs an intended function
definition: A fault prevents this object or process from performing at least one intended function when required. It may still perform other functions. No particular material fracture or physical cause is specified.
example: That is the broken chair. It supports a seated person but cannot hold its back in position.
near: A bell has a hairline crack but still performs every intended function.
reuse: A repair can identify the lost function that is to be restored.

title: completed discovery of a particular target
definition: An experiencer newly identifies a particular target or its whereabouts through an encounter. The resulting change in what the experiencer represents is about that same target. Deliberate searching and physical possession are unspecified.
example: Pip found a cracked bell.
near: Pip already knows where the bell is and only changes an opinion about its colour.
reuse: A later action can involve the very object the finder discovered.

title: onset of awareness of a target
definition: During an episode a cognizer comes to register a particular, distinct target in awareness. The change makes the target present to that cognizer at the time of noticing. The target may be familiar. The means of detection and any subsequent response are unspecified.
example: The keeper noticed a change in the signal.
near: The keeper remained aware of the unchanging signal throughout, with no new moment of noticing.
reuse: Spotting adds the visual source of the change in awareness.
everyday: Became aware of something at that moment

title: visual noticing of a target
parts: onset of awareness of a target
definition: A cognizer comes to notice the target through optical information registered from it during the same episode. The receiver of the optical information is the one who notices. Naming, recognizing or searching for the target is optional.
example: Mira spotted a hairline crack in the lens.
near: Mira noticed the crack by touch in complete darkness.
reuse: Spotting a familiar pattern can add recognition to this visual noticing.

title: route through an interface
definition: An established route connects two sides through an identifiable interface. It can be a physical opening or a defined path between parts of a machine or system. Its availability to any traveler or signal at a particular time is unspecified.
example: The passage linked the outer chamber to the shelter.
near: The two chambers share a wall with no route across it.
reuse: Passable and blocked add different conditions on movement through the same passage.
everyday: A way through from one side to the other

title: passage permitting traversal
definition: At the reference time the passage permits the contextually relevant traveler, signal or other traffic to get through. No actual traversal, invitation, safety guarantee or legal permission is implied.
example: Despite the warning, the service passage was passable.
near: The sign permits entry but a solid barrier prevents the relevant traffic from getting through.
reuse: Reopening adds an earlier blockage and a transition back to this passable condition.

title: passage preventing traversal
definition: At the reference time the passage prevents the contextually relevant traveler, signal or other traffic from getting through. The route can remain identifiable throughout the blockage. The cause, responsibility and duration are unspecified.
example: The gate was blocked by fallen stone.
near: A sign advises against travel but the traveler can still get through.
reuse: Reopening a route can take this condition as its starting point.

title: restoration of passage after blockage
constraints: The first qualifier describes the passage immediately before the transition. The second describes the same passage at its completion for the same kind of traffic. The passage was passable at an earlier time.
definition: A passage that previously permitted the relevant traffic, then prevented it, becomes passable again by the end of the reported transition. Both the earlier and the restored conditions concern the same passage and kind of traffic. No operator or actual traveler is required.
example: After the rubble shifted, the tunnel reopened.
near: Workers opened a new tunnel that had never been passable before.
reuse: A caused reopening can add a distinct actor who brings about this restoration.
everyday: Became passable again after being blocked

title: deliberate inspection of a target
definition: An inspector deliberately evaluates information about a particular target for a relevant condition. The inspection itself is the reported action. Its outcome can be favorable, unfavorable or inconclusive.
example: The technician checked the valve.
near: A sensor noticed a flash without inspecting anything.
reuse: A recheck is another inspection of the same target.
everyday: Examined a target to find out its condition

title: satisfaction of an applicable criterion
definition: A particular result, claim, permit or other bearer meets the criterion applicable to it at the reference time. Continuing validity adds a duration over which that relationship holds.
example: The result is valid.
near: An untested answer is assumed to be acceptable because it exists.
reuse: Continued validity preserves the same bearer and criterion.

title: attainment of an activity endpoint
definition: A process or task attains its relevant endpoint. The endpoint belongs to that activity. A desire, request or prediction can mention completion without committing the speaker to its occurrence.
example: Completion of the scan occurred at noon.
near: The scan began but stopped before the final step.
reuse: A request may take this endpoint as its content.

title: expression asking for an outcome
definition: A requester expresses that an addressee should bring about a specified outcome. The outcome is content of the request. Understanding, agreement and fulfillment each require further evidence.
example: The worker requested a replay.
near: The worker mentioned a replay while describing yesterday.
reuse: A request for completion specifies the requested endpoint.

title: occurrence after a reference event
definition: An event occurs later than a reference event supplied by the context. Temporal succession by itself supplies neither causation nor movement behind another participant.
example: An adjustment followed.
near: A traveler followed a guide along the road.
reuse: A negative quantifier can deny any subsequent occurrence.

title: incorrect judgment by a participant
definition: A bearer holds or expresses a judgment that fails an applicable correctness criterion at the reference time. This reading attributes an error in judgment to the bearer.
example: We were wrong about the source.
near: A person deliberately broke a rule while correctly predicting its effect.
reuse: A later correction can revise this judgment.

title: transition to a traversable passage
definition: A previously nonpassable door, gate or route becomes passable for the relevant traffic by the end of the transition. Its history before this transition is unspecified.
example: The door opened for the first time.
near: A door was passable throughout the reported interval.
reuse: A causing participant can bring about opening of this same passage.

title: convey work between handlers
definition: A source conveys a work assignment or its associated state from one handler to another so that handling can continue. The recipient may be implicit. Physical support or transport of an object is unnecessary.
example: The dispatcher carried the handoffs between two workers.
near: A porter carried a stack of paper without handing work to anyone.
reuse: A handoff may itself be checked before another worker continues.

title: possession of an available resource
definition: At the reference time a holder has a resource in its possession or at its disposal. The bearer can be a group and the resource can be tangible or represented. The relation leaves legal ownership, acquisition and use unspecified.
example: The team has replays.
near: The team knows that replays exist elsewhere but has none.
reuse: An author can quantify the available resources or ask who has them.
everyday: Has a resource at its disposal

title: subsequent inspection of the same target
definition: An inspector inspects the target again after a prior inspection of that target. The inspector in the earlier episode, interval, number of earlier checks and their outcomes are unspecified.
example: The worker rechecked the log.
near: The worker kept looking throughout one uninterrupted inspection.
reuse: An inspection can recur while the target remains valid.

title: continued satisfaction of the same criterion
definition: The same bearer continues to meet the applicable criterion over the reference interval, including its earlier and later portions. The sentence can report this persistence without reporting an inspection.
example: The permit remained valid throughout the change.
near: A previously invalid permit became valid for the first time.
reuse: A later invalidation ends this continued state.
everyday: Continued to meet the same criterion

title: request for attainment of an activity endpoint
definition: A requester communicates a request for an applicable activity to reach its endpoint. The request occurs at its own reference time. The requested completion is embedded content and may never occur.
example: The worker requested completion.
near: The worker reported that the activity had already completed.
reuse: A renewed request can target the same pending completion.
everyday: Asked for the activity to reach its endpoint

title: auditory perception of a target
definition: An experiencer is aware of a target through acoustic input registered from that target during the reference interval. Recognizing its identity or understanding a message is optional.
example: From the hall I can hear the bell.
near: A microphone records the vibration while no one hears it.
reuse: An ability can scope over this perception without asserting that it occurred.

title: visual perception of a target
definition: An experiencer is aware of a target through light registered from that target during the reference interval. No transition from being unaware, identification or interpretation is required.
example: From here Mira can see the tower.
near: The tower first attracts attention when someone mentions it out of view.
reuse: This can be contrasted with the onset of visual noticing.

title: open state of a software resource
definition: A software resource is open for use at the reference time in some application or session. Scope, write permission, who opened it and whether it is being edited are unspecified.
example: The file was open in the editor.
near: The file existed on disk while the application had it closed.
reuse: A later close operation can end this open state.
everyday: Is open for use in software

title: resumption of an interrupted activity
definition: A session or activity that was interrupted begins to proceed again as the same activity. A venue opening to traffic or an unrelated meeting beginning does not establish resumption.
example: After the pause the meeting reopened.
near: A separate meeting began while the original session remained suspended.
reuse: A participant can cause the activity to resume.
